topic: IUPAC naming: root, suffix and prefix
title: IUPAC Naming: Root, Suffix and Prefix
summary: How a chemical name is built from a molecule: the root counts the parent chain's carbons, the suffix gives its bonds and principal group, and the prefix names what is attached.

notes.title: 08 – IUPAC Naming: Root, Suffix and Prefix

keyPoints: **Root:** the number of carbons in the **parent chain**: meth 1, eth 2, prop 3, but 4, pent 5, hex 6.
**Primary suffix:** the bonds in the chain: **-ane** (all single), **-ene** (C=C), **-yne** (C≡C).
**Secondary suffix:** the **principal functional group**: **-ol** (–OH), **-al** (–CHO), **-one** (C=O inside the chain), **-oic acid** (–COOH).
**Prefix:** groups attached to the parent chain: **methyl** (CH₃–), **ethyl** (C₂H₅–), **chloro** (Cl–), **bromo** (Br–), **nitro** (NO₂–).
Number the chain so the **principal group gets the lowest locant**: CH₃–CH(CH₃)–CH₂OH is **2-methylpropan-1-ol**.

blocks.p: The final "e" of -ane is dropped before a suffix that starts with a vowel: propane → propan-1-ol, propanal, propanone.

CH₃–CH(CH₃)–CH₂OH. The longest chain that contains the –OH has 3 carbons → prop. All bonds are single → an. The –OH is the principal group → ol. Numbering from the –OH end puts it on C1 → propan-1-ol. A CH₃ branch sits on C2 → 2-methyl. Name: 2-methylpropan-1-ol.
This page covers the basic logic. Choosing the parent chain when several groups compete, functional-group priority, alphabetical order of prefixes and multiple substituents come next in the series.

quiz.q: The IUPAC name of CH₃–CH(OH)–CH₂–CH₃ is:
quiz.explain: Four carbons, all single bonds, OH on C2 when numbered from the nearer end.

simulation.reason: Naming is a skill students must practise on molecules the reel never names (propene, but-1-ene, propanal, 2-chloropropane, 2-methylbutane, butan-2-ol), and numbering from the wrong end is the commonest mistake: the builder makes the student choose every part and the numbering direction, then shows which part was wrong.
simulation.objective: Build the IUPAC name of each molecule from its root, bonds, suffix, prefix and numbering direction, and see which part decides each piece of the name.
instructions: Count the carbons in the parent chain and pick the root.
Pick the bonds in the chain (an, en or yn).
Pick the principal group (the suffix) and any attached group (the prefix).
Choose which end to number from.
Check your name, then try the next molecule.
